cards.title: The parchi pile is not a system
cards.body: Paper prescriptions fade, tear and go missing. Going digital doesn't have to mean a big software project. Start small.

cards.title: Photograph every prescription
cards.body: With the patient's permission, take a clear photo at the counter. Good light, flat paper, the whole page in frame.

cards.title: Name it so you can find it
cards.body: Patient name and date in the file name or folder. Searching beats flipping through a drawer.

cards.title: Note the key details
cards.body: Medicines, strengths and duration in a simple list. That's what you'll need when refills come around.

cards.title: Double-check the hard-to-read
cards.body: If the handwriting is unclear, call the doctor instead of guessing. A digital copy doesn't fix a misread.

cards.title: Keep it private
cards.body: Prescriptions are personal health information. Keep them on a locked phone or system, never in a group chat.

cards.title: Start with your regulars
cards.body: Digitise long-term patients first, then grow from there. AICA is building AI handwriting reading for pharmacies, now in early pilots in Lucknow.

takeaway: Photograph prescriptions with permission, name files clearly, list key details, confirm unclear handwriting and keep everything private.
share: Send this to the chemist with a shoebox full of parchis.
